observations: Both original languages assert classical reconstruction and the additional same-deck edit-distance lower bound. Neither adds a distinctness or nonisomorphism premise.
SimpleGraph (Fin (n+1)) with 2 <= n represents every finite simple undirected order at least three; isomorphism is used instead of labelled equality.
Cards are induced vertex deletions via succAbove; quotient by graph isomorphism and multiset mapping preserve the meaning and multiplicity of the unlabelled deck.
Edit cost counts each changed unordered pair exactly once, excludes loops, and editDistance is an attained minimum over all vertex bijections.
The identity isomorphism gives zero edit cost and hence zero minimum for every graph paired with itself. The order-three empty graph meets the domain restriction and has the same deck as itself.
The explicit witness refutes ReconstructionRigidity and therefore the complete conjunction OriginalClaim. It does not decide classical Reconstruction.

Challenge theorems verify induced deletion, deck cardinality and multiplicity, isomorphism invariance, distance zero iff isomorphism, unequal labelled isomorphic witnesses, and an actual edit of distance one.
